stem: Why are comprehensive dilated eye examinations important for people at increased risk for glaucoma?

options.A: Glaucoma may have no early symptoms, and a comprehensive dilated eye examination can detect disease before additional irreversible vision loss occurs.
options.B: Glaucoma reliably produces severe eye pain before optic-nerve damage, so examination is unnecessary in an asymptomatic high-risk person.
options.C: A routine blood test detects glaucoma earlier than an eye examination and is the preferred test for people at increased risk.
options.D: Glaucoma develops only after severe central vision loss is present, so examination before visual symptoms has little value.

rationale: NEI states that glaucoma often has no early symptoms, symptoms can progress so slowly that a person may not notice them, and the way to find out whether glaucoma is present is a comprehensive dilated eye examination. NEI's screening statement specifically says detection in higher-risk individuals is best done through a comprehensive dilated eye exam. A is correct.
educational_objective: Explain that glaucoma can be asymptomatic early and that comprehensive dilated eye examination is important for detection in people at increased risk.

audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item accurately states that early disease may be asymptomatic and that comprehensive dilated exam is the high-risk detection approach.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because common glaucoma can be asymptomatic early and does not reliably produce severe pain before damage.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because glaucoma is detected by eye examination, not a routine blood test.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because screening before severe visual symptoms has substantial value.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A matches both the disease presentation and detection recommendation.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives explain the value or non-value of screening in the same risk context.
